sources.entry: Kurenai - Clipboard history with search, saved snippet lists and a paste queue that pastes copied items one by one. Skips passwords, history encrypted on disk. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Lorder19/kurenai) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.name: Kurenai
summary.one_liner: Kurenai is a free, open source clipboard history app for the Mac that keeps copied text and images, supports search, saved snippet lists, and a keyboard-driven paste queue.
use_cases: Recall recently copied text or images
Paste a list of items one by one into a form
Reuse frequently typed replies or addresses
Move a spreadsheet column into a web form
Keep copied items without saving passwords
summary.what_it_does: Kurenai records copied text and images, shown newest first with search. Pressing ⌘1 to ⌘9 pastes one of the top nine items without using the mouse. Saved lists hold frequently reused snippets, with a digit pasting a line. The paste queue makes each ⌘V paste the next copied item. Selecting a column and pressing ⇧⌘C splits it into lines and queues them. Passwords from password managers that mark them as concealed are not saved, and history is encrypted on disk.
notable: Paste queue pastes copied items one at a time with repeated ⌘V
Skips passwords from managers that mark them concealed; ignored-app list includes Keychain Access and Passwords
Windows are marked private so macOS screenshots skip them
Installable via Homebrew cask or direct zip download
caveats: Not signed with an Apple developer certificate, so macOS shows an unidentified developer warning on first open
Encryption key is stored beside the history for the user account, so it protects against a leaked file rather than someone at the Mac
Requires Accessibility permission to press ⌘V; some recording apps ignore the private window flag
